questions: Are you having any difficulty breathing or swallowing?
Has your voice become hoarse, muffled, or different from usual?
Do you feel that your tongue, lips, throat, or neck are swelling?
Do you have blurred vision, double vision, loss of vision, or pain when moving either eye?
Are you unusually drowsy, confused, faint, weak, or having trouble speaking?
Did the swelling begin suddenly over minutes to hours?
Is the swelling rapidly worsening?
Do you have a fever or chills?
Is the forehead or area around either eye severely painful, hot, or tender?
Is one eye swollen more than the other?
Do you have a severe headache, vomiting, or neck stiffness?
Have you recently injured your head or face, even if there is no visible wound?
Have you recently had sinusitis, a dental infection, skin infection, or surgery involving the head or face?
Does the swelling itch or occur with hives or swelling elsewhere?
Have you recently eaten a new food, taken a new medication, or been stung or bitten?
Have you ever had similar episodes of facial or eyelid swelling?
Does the swelling worsen when you bend forward, strain, cough, or lie down?
Do you have swelling of your neck, arms, or both sides of your face?
Are you taking blood thinners or medicines known to cause facial swelling, such as an ACE inhibitor?
Do you have a history of allergies, angioedema, immune-system problems, or cancer?
